seed.text:
00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:12.000 — A sustained, resonant bell tone begins, low and clear, with a slow decay. No speech, no other sounds.

00:00:12.000 --> 00:00:13.000 — The bell tone fades out completely. Silence.

00:00:13.000 --> 00:00:14.000 — A male voice begins speaking: “What is Nirvana?”

00:00:14.000 --> 00:00:20.000 — The same male voice continues: “Nirvana is when everything the mind makes comes to a stop.”

00:00:20.000 --> 00:00:25.000 — The male voice continues: “The letting go of everything carried, the thirst ends, nothing pulls you anymore, stopping.”

00:00:25.000 --> 00:00:28.000 — The male voice continues: “Going out like a flame with no fuel.”

00:00:28.000 --> 00:00:30.000 — A female voice begins speaking: “This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.”

00:00:30.000 --> 00:00:32.000 — The female voice continues: “Why don’t I see Nirvana right now?”

00:00:32.000 --> 00:00:35.000 — The male voice resumes: “You do not see Nirvana right now because you imagine a seer and a world, and neither is there.”

00:00:35.000 --> 00:00:38.000 — The male voice continues: “What is called ‘manana’ is the imagining in egoistic terms, imparting reality to illusory things.”

00:00:38.000 --> 00:00:42.000 — The male voice continues: “Only a looking is there, nothing worth looking at. Only a seeing is there, nothing to be seen.”

00:00:42.000 --> 00:00:45.000 — The male voice continues: “The law of dependent arising is already implicated. There is therefore no seer apart from the phenomenon of seeing, according to the Tathagata.”

00:00:45.000 --> 00:00:47.000 — The female voice asks: “What keeps it going?”

00:00:47.000 --> 00:00:50.000 — The male voice answers: “Thirst keeps it going, impelled by that making it into something, it runs towards the mirage, the gap is ignored.”

00:00:50.000 --> 00:00:53.000 — The male voice continues: “What impels one to ignore that gap is thirst.”

00:00:53.000 --> 00:00:55.000 — The female voice asks: “Perception. What impels one to ignore that gap is craving.”

0

s1.text:
00:00.000–00:02.500: A sustained, high-pitched electronic tone, pure sine wave, centered in the stereo field, no speech, no background noise.

00:02.500–00:03.500: The tone ends abruptly. Silence for 0.5 seconds.

00:03.500–00:10.000: A male voice speaks clearly, mid-range pitch, slightly reverberant, saying: “Nirvana is when everything the mind makes comes to a stop.”

00:10.000–00:16.000: The same male voice continues: “The letting go of everything carried, the thirst ends, nothing pulls you anymore, stopping, going out like a flame with no fuel.”

00:16.000–00:20.000: Silence for 4 seconds. No speech, no background noise.

00:20.000–00:27.000: A different male voice, slightly lower pitch, more measured, says: “This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.”

00:27.000–00:30.000: Silence for 3 seconds. No speech, no background noise.

00:30.000–00:45.000: A third male voice, with a more academic or analytical tone, says: “There seems to be some contradiction in the commentarial definitions of nibbana. On the one hand, we have the definition of nibbana as the exit from craving which is called a weaving, and on the other it is said that it is on seeing nibbana the craving is destroyed. To project nibbana into a distance and to hope that craving will be destroyed only on seeing it is something like trying to build a staircase to a palace one cannot yet see.”

00:45.000–00:50.000: Silence for 5 seconds. No speech, no background noise.

00:50.000–01:00.000: A fourth male voice, with a formal, almost recitative cadence, says: “In fact, this is a simile in which the Buddha had used in his criticism of the Brahmins’ point of view. In the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta we have a very clear statement of the third noble truth, having first said that the second noble truth is craving, the Buddha goes on to define the third noble truth in these words: ‘Tassa yeva tanhā asesā’.”

01:00.000–01:01.000: The voice ends abruptly. Silence for 1 second.

No clicks, thumps, or glitches. No sudden volume jumps. No synthetic or robotic voices. No speech starts or ends mid-sentence within the recorded segments.

(a) speech starting or ending mid-sentence:  
— 00:00.000 — 00:02.100: “There seems to be some contradiction in the commentarial definitions of Nibbana, on the one hand we have the definition of Nibbana as the exit from craving which is called...”  
— 00:15.300 — 00:17.800: “...on seeing Nibbana, craving is destroyed. To project Nibbana into a distance and to hope that craving will be destroyed only on seeing it...”  
— 00:27.400 — 00:30.100: “...is something like trying to build a staircase to a palace one cannot yet see.”  
— 00:34.200 — 00:37.600: “In fact, this is a simile in which the Buddha had used in his criticism of the Brahmins’ point of view.”  
— 00:44.100 — 00:47.300: “In the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta we have a very clear statement of the third noble truth...”  
— 00:52.800 — 00:56.200: “...having first said that the second noble truth is craving, the Buddha goes on to define the third noble truth in these words:”  
— 01:00.100 — 01:03.500: “‘Tassa yeva tanhāyā asesāviraġanirōdho...’”  
— 01:07.200 — 01:11.800: “...this is to say that the third noble truth is the complete fading away, cessation, giving up, relinquishment of that very craving...”  
— 01:17.300 — 01:20.700: “...that it is the release from and non-attachment to that very craving. In other words, it is the destruction of this very mass of suffering which is just before us.”  
— 01:28.100 — 01:31.400: “In the Sutta...”  
— 01:33.200 — 01:36.800: “...on the extinction of fetters to existence. This is the highest knowledge, this is the unsurpassed bliss, this sorrowless, stainless security is the supreme and deathlessness.”

(b) silence longer than 5 seconds where speech should be:  
— None observed.

(c) clicks, thumps, or glitches:  
— None observed.

(d) sudden volume jumps between voices:  
— None observed; only one voice throughout.

(e) synthetic or robotic voices:  
— None observed; natural human voice with consistent tone and pacing.

Note: All speech is delivered by a single speaker with no interruptions, background noise, or audio artifacts. No voice changes occur. The speaker quotes Pali phrases mid-sentence, but no other voices or tonal shifts are present.
